1.explanation:
• audits/byte-efficiency/unminified-javascript-test.js tests the Minify JavaScript audit logic (this is where duplicated stack packs appear in the Byte Efficiency category).
• audits/dobetterweb/js-libraries-test.js covers the js-libraries audit (Best Practices) which surfaces stack pack data for libraries like React.
• report/html/renderer/category-renderer-test.js verifies how stack packs are rendered in the HTML report (so you can confirm duplicate entries show up in the UI).
• runner-test.js shows how Lighthouse orchestrates gathering, auditing, and stack-pack collection at runtime—useful for reproducing the end-to-end flow.
• network-records-to-devtools-log.js is used to turn networkRecords into a DevTools log for audits like Minify JavaScript (you’ll need this when building a test fixture against abcnews.go.com).
• create-test-trace.js lets you generate a synthetic trace to feed into Lighthouse’s audit runner, completing the artifacts needed to repro the issue locally.
1.bug_scenario: When you run Lighthouse (or PageSpeed Insights) against https://abcnews.go.com/ and inspect the “Minify JavaScript” audit, you see two identical React stack-pack entries. In the UI you get two React icons and two copies of the same advice. In the raw JSON (__LIGHTHOUSE_JSON__) the `stackPacks` array contains two entries both with `{id: 'react', title: 'React'}`, one from the standard detector and one from the new “Fast Path” checks introduced by the js-library-detector update.
